settings.prompt: Take three test tubes, and add 2 mL of unfermented milk, fermenting milk, and fermented milk to each, respectively. Add two drops of bromothymol blue indicator to each tube.

Immerse full-rooted maize seedlings in a container filled with red dye solution. After a period of time-lapse photography, remove one seedling and horizontally cut its stem with a blade. The structure of the cross-section is clearly visible, with particular emphasis on the internal vascular tissue structure.

On the workbench, there is a simple RC charging circuit: a battery, switch, and resistor are connected in series to charge a capacitor, and an LED is connected in parallel across the capacitor's two terminals; one hand toggles the switch to connect the battery.
Take 2 mL of soymilk into a test tube, add 1 mL of reagent A of the biuret test, shake thoroughly to mix, then add 4 drops of reagent B, and shake again.
Two transparent glass jars containing turbid muddy water are placed side by side; salt is added to the right jar. After both jars are briefly stirred, they are left undisturbed.
On the desk, a rotary potentiometer is connected in series with a small incandescent lamp; a hand slowly rotates the knob back and forth.
Fixed infrared cameras captured two adjacent surfaces under noon sunlight: the left one was a dark asphalt pavement, and the right one was a green lawn, recording their temperature changes over time.

Drop two soil samples from the same height onto the ground, where sample A is pure clay and sample B is a mixture of lime and clay. Subsequently, observe and compare the damage experienced by sample A and sample B.

Use two sandboxes filled with loose sand. A static pressure (weight of X) is applied to sandbox A, while a shock pressure of the same weight X is applied to sandbox B. Observe and compare the density and height of the sand in both sandboxes.

Using acoustic wave ripples (waveforms) to represent sound propagation, show sound waves traveling outward from a source toward a sponge block and a glass pane placed side by side, and continuing past each material to the far side.

Three large samples—rock wool (pale yellow), steel (silver gray), and wood (brown)—are displayed side by side, with dynamic red heat flow arrows indicating the rate of heat transfer. The focus of the image is on the contrasting movement speeds of the red arrows on the three samples.

A mass-spring-damper system hangs vertically, suspended from a fixed frame above a workbench; a hand strikes the mass block with a rubber hammer briefly and then removes it, so that the mass is no longer subjected to external forces.
On the test bench, a microphone is connected to an AM transmitter and antenna; when a person speaks softly and then loudly into the microphone, the oscilloscope displays the corresponding signals.

In the wind tunnel, a thin airfoil is horizontally installed, and smoke lines are continuously injected upstream under steady airflow conditions, while the airfoil is gradually rotated to increase the angle of attack.

On the experimental bench, two petri dishes contain latex beads coated with antigen; a gloved hand uses a pipette with a red tip to add liquid to the left side and a pipette with a blue tip to add liquid to the right side, then gently agitates both.

B lymphocytes are detected by surface antibody staining. The procedure involves adding labeled antibodies to a prepared cell suspension, gently mixing, incubating, washing, and then observing under a fluorescence microscope or flow cytometer.
A person is facing the camera, with one hand holding a bag and delivering a brief puff of air near one eye from the side.

Place the starch solution into two test tubes separately. Add fresh saliva to one test tube and distilled water to the other. Let both test tubes stand undisturbed for a short period. Then add iodine solution drop by drop to both test tubes. Demonstrate the clear and simple hand operations using test tubes and pipettes.

Two identical transparent beakers containing equal volumes of room temperature water are placed side by side; the beaker on the left is added with crystalline sugar, and the beaker on the right is added with sugar glass fragments, both being stirred gently with the same force.

Two identical transparent beakers are placed side by side, each containing still distilled water; at the same time, liposome-encapsulated blue dye is added to the left beaker, and free blue dye is added to the right beaker.

Transfer an appropriate amount of erythromycin reagent solution into a test tube. Slowly add concentrated sulfuric acid along the inner wall of the test tube using a pipette. Keep the test tube upright, gently shake to mix the contents, and observe the progress of the reaction inside the test tube.
A clean forearm is displayed. A hand with a smooth pad rubs the same skin area back and forth with moderate force for several seconds, then stops, and the skin is left exposed for observation.

Demonstrate delayed dermographism. Select the forearm of a healthy adult for the procedure. Use a blunt stick to draw a straight line on the skin with moderate pressure. After an interval representing the multi-hour delay characteristic of this reaction (shown here in compressed form), re-examine the marked area. Clearly demonstrate the entire procedure step by step.
In a transparent glass bowl containing warm milk, slowly add vinegar while gently stirring with a spoon.
Freeze whole strawberries and thaw them at room temperature; show a close-up image of the thawed strawberries being gently pressed or cut open.
A bar magnet is pushed into and pulled out of a copper wire coil connected to a galvanometer, whose needle is clearly visible.
A negatively charged gold-leaf electroscope, equipped with a zinc plate at its top, is illuminated by a lamp that alternately emits light in the visible and ultraviolet ranges at the same distance.
Place two identical jars side by side, each containing water and a layer of oil; add dish soap only to the right jar, seal both jars, and shake them vigorously.
Two transparent beakers are placed side by side: one contains a starch suspension, and the other contains cellulose fibers; iodine solution is added to both.
Two African sunbirds are displayed side by side, with the female on the left and the male on the right. Observe and compare the morphological differences between these two sunbirds.
Mark the sex of two woodpeckers. Use a pointing rod to indicate the color and morphological differences in the red crown feathers between males and females.
Two adjacent transparent beakers: red heat-stable catalase and blue regular catalase are heated in a water bath, followed by the simultaneous addition of hydrogen peroxide.

On an experimental bench, two test tubes with blue and red caps are present; a gloved hand adds DNA template, nucleotides, and RNA polymerase to the blue-capped tube, after which both tubes are placed under ultraviolet light.

A male robin perches on a branch, engaged in a courtship interaction with a female robin perched on an adjacent branch. Fixed camera position, natural outdoor lighting, continuous unedited recording, no narration or text overlay.
Two shallow soil trays were placed side by side, one planted with wetland vegetation and the other bare; the same turbid water was poured into both, flowing into the transparent containers below.
Live-cell fluorescence microscopy imaging of cultured mammalian cells expressing a green fluorescent glucocorticoid receptor; glucocorticoid hormone was added only to the left well during imaging.
A microcentrifuge tube containing cell culture lysate was removed from a benchtop centrifuge immediately after a complete high-speed spin and held upright, motionless, in hand.

On the experimental bench, a transparent beaker containing cell-free microbial culture medium was gently stirred, and then a concentrated salt solution was added. After stopping the stirring, the beaker was left undisturbed.
A cold, flat metal plate placed on a table is gently blown over by warm, humid air.
A sealed, transparent plastic bottle with a small pool of water at its base and clear air inside is squeezed firmly by hand and then suddenly released.
A clear tank with a small vibration source fixed at the central position just below the water surface; it continuously transmits vibrations into the water when activated.
A porous sponge sample was placed in a beaker. Calcium carbonate solution was then gradually poured in until the sponge's base was fully submerged.
A small tray with a slight inclination contains soil and small pebbles. Water is continuously poured from the higher end, causing the water to flow across the tray and exit from the lower side.
In a dark room, place a calcite or fluorite mineral on the table and repeatedly expose it to a handheld ultraviolet lamp by turning it on and off.
In a shallow seawater tray, dark crude oil was poured onto the water surface, with a clean bird feather floating nearby. The water surface was gently disturbed by slow hand movements.
Immerse a dry, unglazed ceramic shard in a glass container filled with clear, still water and allow it to stand for several minutes.

Two model roofs are placed side by side, with the left one having a gentler slope and the right one a steeper slope, both constructed from the same material. Subsequently, the same white granular material is spread onto both roofs. The camera focuses on the process of the white granular material sliding down the surfaces of the two roofs.

The video first presents the karst dissolution landscape in Guilin, followed by the karst dissolution landscape in Croatia. The focus is on the differences in morphology between these two limestone landscapes.
Side by side, two dynamic images are presented: the left one shows the flowing pattern of advection fog, and the right one shows the flowing pattern of radiation fog.

Input a low-frequency sound signal and display its waveform. Keep the amplitude constant while gradually increasing the frequency of the sound. As the frequency increases, observe the periodic changes in the waveform on the screen.
A speaker uses speech analysis software with a real-time spectrogram, continuously produces a vowel into the microphone, then pauses briefly, and subsequently produces a stop consonant.
On the green, a player gently strikes a golf ball with a putter, sending it rolling across the putting surface toward the hole.
The athlete swims freestyle toward the wall, lowers the head, pulls the knees in for a forward flip turn, pushes off the wall, and adjusts the posture before continuing to swim forward.
Place a fresh male pumpkin flower on a tray, remove the petals with forceps, and then longitudinally dissect the flower with a scalpel to expose its internal structure.

Show a hand holding a dry soybean seed. Use forceps to remove the seed coat. Separate and open the seed to expose its internal structure. The procedure is clear and the steps are logical, with a focus on seed dissection.

Display a whole dried corn kernel placed on a flat surface. Use a sharp blade to longitudinally cut the corn kernel from the top to the bottom. Separate the two halves so that both cut faces are fully visible to the camera.

Place a fresh corn leaf flat on a table, gently smooth it with fingers, and observe its surface from above to demonstrate the plant's morphology. Highlight its elongated leaf shape and illustrate the multiple veins arranged from the leaf base to the leaf tip.
Pipette 2 mL of fish liver oil extract into a dry test tube, and add 3 mL of antimony trichloride-chloroform solution. Mix thoroughly.

Weigh 5 grams of tomato homogenate into a beaker, add 10 mL of acetone for extraction. After filtration, transfer the filtrate into a cuvette and measure the absorbance at 503 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Add 2 mL yeast extract solution to a test tube, then add 2 drops of acidic ferric chloride–hydroxylamine (hydroxamate) color reagent and mix thoroughly.
Add 2 mL of rice extract to a test tube, then add an alkaline potassium ferricyanide solution. Mix thoroughly and expose to a UV lamp.
Take 2 mL of pig liver extract and place it in a test tube, then add sodium diethyldithiocarbamate solution.
Pipette 2 mL of the yolk extract into a test tube, add ammonium molybdate solution and ascorbic acid, and heat in a boiling water bath for 2 minutes.

Both glass cups are filled with a milky-white latex colloidal suspension; add a spoonful of salt to the cup on the right and stir, while keeping the cup on the left unchanged. Place both cups within the field of vision.
A piece of chocolate is placed on a slightly heated metal pan, and it is continuously recorded for several minutes while being heated.

Two identical LED–resistor–capacitor branches are placed side by side: the left branch contains a capacitor with a red housing, which is pre-charged and then disconnected; the right branch contains a capacitor with a blue housing, which is uncharged; a single switch connects both branches to their respective LEDs.
On the workbench, a microcontroller's DAC drives an LED through an RC filter, and the program continuously updates the DAC value.
A desk lamp is connected to a PIR motion sensor located at the door. A person opens the door, enters, pauses for a moment, stands still, and then leaves.
A row of LEDs connected to a shift register, equipped with a visible clock button or knob and a fixed data source; a hand repeatedly triggers the clock.
A transparent vertical tube filled with dry fine sand is placed upright, with its bottom immersed in a shallow pan of water, and observed from the side over time.

Two sandboxes were used. Three model piles were placed in sandbox A and filled with sandy soil, while sandbox B was filled with sandy soil only. Equal weights were applied on the top of both sandboxes and they were fixed on a shaking table. Subsequently, the vibration was initiated, and the settlement of the load was observed and compared between sandbox A and sandbox B.
On a table, two adjacent trays containing coarse sand and fine dust are placed; a household fan is blowing continuously on them for several seconds.

Three glass cups filled with distilled water are placed side by side: a tablet is placed in the cup on the left, a capsule is placed in the middle cup, and a liquid medication is poured into the cup on the right.

Prepare three test tubes, each containing an equal volume of hydrogen peroxide solution. Add a lipid oxidation indicator to each test tube. The first test tube receives no selenium, the second test tube is supplemented with a low concentration selenium solution, and the third test tube is supplemented with a higher concentration selenium solution. Gently mix all test tubes and place them side by side for comparison.
Place liquid egg white in a test tube and heat it in a water bath while gently shaking. Only show the steps involving the thermometer, beaker, test tube, and controlled heating.

Add equal volumes of water and edible oil to a transparent test tube. Add a small amount of emulsifier. Seal the test tube, vigorously shake it for several seconds, then place the test tube upright and observe over time. Clearly demonstrate the experimental procedure, equipment used, and operational methods.

Display a simple binary tree on a light background, with nodes labeled (1–7); highlight the nodes from top to bottom according to their level using bright colors (e.g., red) to demonstrate level order traversal. Briefly illuminate each node when visited, and add a mark for it — its numeral if legible digits can be rendered, otherwise a simple tally mark or dot — to the left-to-right output list at the bottom of the screen.
Take 2 mL of an irrigation water sample containing chloride ions into a test tube and add 2 drops of silver nitrate solution.
First, sketch a simple sphere. Apply the gradient technique to draw smooth transitional areas of light and shadow on the sphere, keeping the light source direction fixed as the shading is applied.
Take 2 mL of the plant oil extract into a test tube, add 2 drops of ethanol solution of phosphomolydic acid, and heat for 1 minute in a boiling water bath.

Two identical inclined planes are placed side by side, with an eraser on the left and a metal block on the right. The angle of inclination of the planes is increased simultaneously, and then both objects are released to slide down at the same time.
A circular eardrum sprinkled with fine sand is continuously driven by a mechanical vibrator at a fixed frequency during vibration.
A shallow water wave tank contains a rigid barrier with two narrow, parallel slits. A single planar wave travels across the water surface toward the barrier and reaches the two slits.

Capture a bicycle wheel with evenly spaced spokes rotating at a constant speed: first record with a lower frame rate, then with a higher frame rate, keeping the wheel rotational speed and camera position the same.

Mark the north (N) and south (S) poles of two identical bar magnets. Hold one magnet with its north pole facing the south pole of the other magnet, and bring them close together. Then release your hands and observe the state of the magnets.

A triangular glass prism is placed in a beam of sunlight, allowing the light to pass through it. Observe what happens to the light as it exits the prism, noting the appearance, distribution, and order of any colors that result.
A vertical soap film is formed on a rectangular metal frame, illuminated by stable white light, while the soap film flows slowly and the frame is gently tilted.

In a dimly lit room, align a red laser pointer and a white LED flashlight side by side toward a rough wall. Keep the wall and camera stationary. First gently oscillate the laser pointer by itself while the flashlight stays still; then pause, and gently oscillate the LED flashlight by itself while the laser pointer stays still.
Place a ceramic tile on the left side of the table, and a similar metal plate on the right side. Place ice cubes of the same size at the center of each, and record under the same indoor conditions.

Physics demonstration experiment: A bar magnet is sequentially brought close to three materials—nail, copper wire, and aluminum sheet. The hand moves the magnet one by one close to each object on the table. The procedure is simple, clear, and sequential.
Time-lapse photography of sodium chloride crystal formation in a shallow salt solution within a transparent glass dish as water evaporates.

Two identical paper strips are placed side by side: the left one is immersed in blue water, and the right one is immersed in yellow cooking oil. The movement of the liquid upward along the paper strips over time is observed.
A glass liquid thermometer is placed in a beaker containing water on a hot plate, and then transferred to a second beaker containing cold water.
A stainless steel plate is heated from below, while milk continuously flows over its surface under continuous heating.

Place a metal spoon and a wooden spoon side by side in the same transparent container filled with hot water, and place a small equal amount of butter on the handles of each spoon above the water surface.

On the table, small neodymium cube magnets, each marked with a small colored dot on one face, are arranged in a checkerboard pattern so that neighboring magnets show the dot facing up or down in alternation, and then a thin square piece of pyrolytic graphite is released above the array.
On the table, there are two coils, one with an iron core and one without a core, sharing the same power supply and located above a steel washer; the power supply is turned on and off simultaneously.

A hard glass test tube contains black carbon powder. An excess of concentrated sulfuric acid is added, and the test tube is heated with an alcohol lamp. The gas generated is led through a delivery tube into a fuchsin solution.
A sealed plastic bag containing vinegar and baking soda is placed on a balance; the reactants are mixed inside the bag.
A conical flask containing an iodine solution and starch indicator is shaken while sodium thiosulfate solution is added from a burette.
A white filter paper is standing upright in a transparent container, with a black marker dot near the bottom, whose lower edge is in contact with the water surface, and water is penetrating upward.

A transparent glass cuvette containing guaiacol and hydrogen peroxide was prepared. Horseradish peroxidase was added using a pipette, followed by gentle shaking of the cuvette. The reaction was recorded by side-view photography.
A test tube containing orange acidic potassium dichromate solution is treated with ethanol solution and then shaken.

Two test tubes are placed side by side: the left test tube contains ferric chloride solution, into which sodium hydroxide solution is added; the right test tube contains ferrous sulfate solution, into which sodium hydroxide solution is also added.
A test tube contains colorless dilute hydrochloric acid, into which a silvery magnesium strip is placed.
A test tube contains a small amount of yellowish sodium peroxide powder. Distilled water is added, a glowing splint is inserted, and phenolphthalein solution is dropped in.
A pipette is dripping sodium alginate solution into a beaker containing a calcium chloride solution on the laboratory bench, and the solution is gently stirred as more droplets are added.

Place two identical transparent glass containers side by side: the left one containing water and the right one containing clear edible oil. Add an equal small amount of salt to each container, and gently shake them.
Place the wolframite powder in a test tube, add hot concentrated hydrochloric acid to dissolve it, then add a few drops of stannous chloride solution, followed by potassium thiocyanate solution.
In the laboratory, the impure copper(II) sulfate crystals were dissolved in hot water on a hot plate, and the solution was filtered into a clean beaker and allowed to cool by standing.
Add ethyl bromide and aqueous sodium hydroxide to a test tube, heat to boiling, cool, acidify with nitric acid, and then add silver nitrate solution.

Two transparent beakers are placed side by side, each containing identical metal electrodes, a battery, and a light bulb in a circuit; one beaker contains pure water, while the other contains water with dissolved salt, and the circuits are then simultaneously closed.
Place a slice of raw potato and a slice of fresh apple side by side on a dish, and add iodine solution to the surfaces of both using a pipette.
Freshly cut Elodea stems were submerged in a transparent container and placed under bright light. A non-transparent card was briefly used to block the light, then removed.
A potted Mimosa plant, after a human finger gently touches one of the leaflets on a compound leaf, is presented in a stable close-up shot.
Macrophage-like cells in a dish were observed under a microscope over time after red and green plastic beads were added to the surrounding liquid.
Place a fresh Elodea leaf on a microscope slide with a drop of water, cover it with a coverslip, and observe the leaf cells under an optical microscope for several minutes.
Two transparent chambers containing moist air are placed side by side; cigarette smoke is introduced only into the left chamber, and then both chambers are rapidly cooled simultaneously.
A person exhales breath through a tube into a transparent glass container holding a clear calcium hydroxide solution, with the tube's submerged end reaching below the liquid surface.
A lit incense stick is placed between two identical metal plates, one heated and the other cooled, allowing smoke to rise freely above both.
On a worktable, quartz and pink feldspar are placed side by side; a hand first uses the quartz to scratch the feldspar, and then uses the feldspar to attempt to scratch the quartz.

On the table, a handheld analog magnetometer with a visible pointer remains stable, while a red-and-blue striped bar magnet is brought close to it from the side, moved away, and then flipped once (180°); the whole approach–move-away–flip sequence is then repeated once more.

A person holds a portable compass and walks in a straight line over exposed soil, sweeping left and right above a buried ferromagnetic object (e.g., iron or steel), then repeats the process from the opposite direction.
Take 1 mL of the extracted water sample and place it into a quartz cuvette. Position the cuvette under a fluorescence spectrophotometer with an excitation wavelength of 365 nm.

Prepare two test tubes containing lactose solution. Add lactase to one test tube and leave the other as a control without enzyme. Incubate both test tubes at a warm temperature. After incubation, add Benedict's reagent and gently heat. Clearly demonstrate the step-by-step procedure using test tubes, pipettes, water bath, and heating apparatus.
Two identical ice cubes are placed side by side; calcium chloride is sprinkled on the left one, and sodium chloride is sprinkled on the right one, then observed for several minutes.

Build a simple circuit consisting of a battery, a switch, and a light bulb. First, connect a copper wire of fixed length into the circuit and close the switch. Then replace it with an iron wire of the same length and reconnect the circuit. Clearly demonstrate the comparison process, emphasizing the correct wiring sequence and maintaining consistent conditions.

Position a book upright in front of a vertical plane mirror so that both the book and its reflection are visible in frame. Slowly move the book toward the mirror, then move it back to its starting position, while the camera and mirror remain fixed.
A opaque cup with a coin at the bottom is placed on a table; the camera is fixed at the same height as the table. Keep the camera stationary and slowly pour water into the cup.

Two identical transparent glass cups are placed side by side: one contains ice water, and the other is steaming. Two identical effervescent tablets are simultaneously dropped, one into each cup, from a stable frontal perspective.
Place two identical steel wool pads on a ceramic dish; pour hydrogen peroxide onto the left pad while keeping the right one dry, and capture images of both from the same angle continuously.
An infrared thermal imaging camera shows a desktop: a bare hand is placed flat on the table for several seconds, then lifted away from the surface.
Two test tubes containing Lucas reagent: the left tube was added with tert-butyl alcohol, and the right tube was added with ethanol. After gentle shaking, they were left at room temperature.

A circuit powered by a battery and connected through a small motor links metal electrodes placed in two transparent beakers positioned side by side: the left one contains saltwater, and the right one contains distilled water, with current passing through each beaker separately.
A small piece of silvery aluminum foil was placed into a test tube containing 5 mL of colorless dilute hydrochloric acid.

Two adjacent transparent test tubes, one colorless and the other colored, contain catalase; hydrogen peroxide is added to both simultaneously, with the colored tube containing an inhibitor, and the camera remains stationary.

On the lab bench, two clear test tubes containing fructose-1,6-bisphosphate: the left one contains the active enzyme, and the right one contains the heat-denatured enzyme. After brief incubation, a molybdate-based phosphate detection reagent was added.

Place two identical transparent sealed chambers side by side, with the left one marked in red and the right one marked in blue; introduce steam into the red chamber while keeping the blue chamber dry, and then cool both chambers simultaneously.

The screen first displayed a satellite view of the American Plateau, followed by a satellite view of a mountain range in Asia. The visual compared the differences in color and morphology between the two regions through satellite imagery.

First, a large map of the Asian marine basins is presented, showing surface ocean currents driven by wind and the Coriolis force with arrows. Subsequently, a map of inland lakes in Europe is shown, illustrating surface water movements driven by local winds with arrows. The formation processes and flow directions of these two types of currents are clearly demonstrated through distinct arrows and a top-down perspective.

On the table, place two metal tuning forks of different sizes above a shallow, transparent trough of still water. Strike the first fork with a mallet and lower its prongs into the water; once that fork is vibrating in the water, strike the second fork with the same mallet motion and lower its prongs into the water at the same depth, so both forks' effects on the water are visible together.
First, a brightly colored Amazon parrot is presented, followed by a Congo parrot. The two birds are displayed in sequence, highlighting their size and feather coloration as key characteristics.
A speaker sits at a table with a burning candle placed a few centimeters in front of their mouth, alternately producing voiced and voiceless stop syllables toward the flame.

Outdoors in a gentle breeze, with a wind indicator such as nearby grass or a hanging fabric ribbon visibly swaying to mark the wind, two identically configured microphones are mounted side by side and face the same direction as gusts pass through: one microphone is left fully exposed, the other is enclosed in a thick foam windscreen. Each microphone feeds its own visible audio level meter (an analog VU needle or digital waveform display) placed in frame beside its stand, showing the incoming signal in real time.
A long jumper sprints, takes off with one leg, completes a standard and complete triple jump, and lands with both feet in the sand pit. The entire movement is clearly and smoothly presented.

The figure shows a coordinate axis, with the horizontal axis representing output and the vertical axis representing average cost. A curve is plotted in the figure, illustrating how costs change with increasing output under conditions of diseconomies of scale.

A set of axes is displayed on the screen, with the horizontal axis representing budget category and the vertical axis representing amount. Under conditions of fiscal deficit, a bar chart is created to represent income and expenditure.

A concise 2D animation illustrates an array of numbered boxes arranged horizontally (e.g., [5, 1, 2, 4, 3]), with a highlighted pointer moving from left to right to perform a sequential search for a target value (e.g., 4).

The figure shows a coordinate axis, with the horizontal axis representing quantity and the vertical axis representing cost. A marginal cost curve is plotted on the coordinate axis, and the marginal cost point A is labeled.

Prepare two soil samples, labeled as acidic and alkaline, respectively. Calibrate a handheld pH meter. Insert the probe into the moist acidic soil, wait for the reading to stabilize, then clean the probe. Insert the probe into the moist alkaline soil and wait for the reading to stabilize. The pH value is displayed as a numerical value on the instrument screen.
